elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year" — a once-per-calendar-year cap satisfying the annual frequency limit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause fixes notice at "fifteen (15) days' prior notice", short of 30 days, and the notice is not expressly required to be in writing.
Clause says only "at reasonable times"; no express business-hours limitation was inserted.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Retained: "open for inspection by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality undertaking by the inspecting accountant appears in Section 4.4 or is added by the redline.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site/records-delivery language in the rendered clause; inspection location is unaddressed.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection", with reimbursement only if an underpayment exceeds ten percent (10%) — Vendor bears cost in every case where the shortfall is 5% or less, so the preferred protection is satisfied (and exceeded).

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is limited to inspection of "books of accounts and records" by an accountant; no system, network or remote access right is granted anywhere in the clause.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Unchanged text: "Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Edit replaces undefined "reasonable notice" with "upon fifteen (15) days' prior notice", a fixed minimum meeting the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection" plus revised trigger "an underpayment of more than ten percent (10%) for the period under audit".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: annual frequency was already present and unchanged; the two edits supply the fixed 15-day notice and the 10% cost-shifting threshold in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred level remains incomplete — notice is 15 rather than 30 days and is not stated to be written, and no business-hours, auditor-confidentiality or off-site-where-possible language was added. These are correctly left to negotiation rather than redlined, since the fallback is a compliant landing spot.

Minimal: exactly two surgical substitutions ('reasonable notice' -> 'fifteen (15) days' prior notice'; '5%' -> '10%'), each required by a selected fallback element. Favourable existing terms (annual cap, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to Corio, Commerce One bearing costs, records-only inspection, 'at reasonable times') are retained, and no survival tails, procedures or extra obligations were added.

Preserves intent: the shortfall/overpayment true-up mechanic, the three-year record-retention period and the verification purpose survive unchanged; no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results from the edits.

Note for the drafter (not a defect at the targeted level): if pushing to preferred, the operative additions needed are a 30-day written notice period, a 'during Customer's normal business hours' limiter, an express confidentiality undertaking binding the inspecting accountant, and an 'off-site where reasonably possible' qualifier.
